Preprint
Mathematical Physics

Closed forms for the constants in the odd-weight identities
between dihedral modular graph functions
Noah Schittenhelm
Hack-Nation 2026, Team Ninja Turtles
Preprint, October 2026

Abstract We consider the combinations Xw of twoloop dihedral modular graph functions C(a, b, c) of odd
weight w whose hyperbolic Laplacian is a multiple of the
Eisenstein series E(w). At each odd weight examined,
3 ≤ w ≤ 61, we prove Xw = fw E(w) + gw ζ(w) with
fw = 3((w − 1)/2)!/w and gw = 6|Bw−1 |/((w − 1)/2)!.
The proof combines exact Laplace algebra, a harmonicity, invariance and growth argument, and a constant
term evaluated from a Laurent polynomial in rational
arithmetic. It assumes a theorem of D’Hoker–Kaidi and
a standard lemma, neither checked by code. We also
show exactly that at each weight 3 ≤ w ≤ 25 the space
of combinations with ∆X ∈ QE(w) has dimension 1 for
odd w and 0 for even w. Independently of the proof,
the constants at w = 3, . . . , 17 are confirmed numerically at 32 digits at verifier-chosen points, and w = 17
was a preregistered blind test. The full weight-11 basis
has exactly one relation, established numerically by a
singular-value criterion. A proof beyond the examined
range remains open.

Difficulty. The Laplace equation alone leaves gw
undetermined [1]. Fixing it requires the Laurent polynomial of each C(a, b, c) at the cusp. The size of the
combination grows with w, and numerical searches for
relations are limited by the working precision relative
to the height of the coefficients.
Contribution. The Laurent polynomial of each single Cu,v;w is known (Theorem 5.1 of D’Hoker–Kaidi,
arXiv:1902.04180). We evaluate it in rational arithmetic on the DGV combinations. This gives closed
forms for fw and gw with a proof at each odd weight examined, w ≤ 61, together with numerical confirmations
independent of that proof.
Summary of results.
• Theorem 1 shows Xw = fw E(w) + gw ζ(w) exactly
at each odd weight examined, 3 ≤ w ≤ 61, with
fw and gw in closed form. The proof is computerassisted in rational arithmetic, and its assumptions
are stated openly.
• Theorem 2 shows that the space {X : ∆X ∈
QE(w)} is one-dimensional for odd w and zero
for even w, at each weight 3 ≤ w ≤ 25.
• Conjecture 1 states that the closed forms persist
beyond the examined range; they are proved up to
w = 61.
• Observations 1 to 3 confirm numerically, independently of the proof, the constants at w = 3, . . . , 17.
They show that the full weight-11 basis carries exactly one relation. They also report a hardening
run that exposed and fixed one evaluator bug.

Keywords Modular graph functions · Laplace eigenvalue equations · Eisenstein series · Bernoulli numbers ·
Genus-one string amplitudes · Computer-assisted proof

1 Introduction
Two-loop dihedral modular graph functions C(a, b, c)
appear as coefficients in the low-energy expansion of
the one-loop amplitude of closed strings. D’Hoker,
Green and Vanhove showed that they satisfy Laplace
eigenvalue equations with inhomogeneous terms polynomial in non-holomorphic Eisenstein series, and that
the Laplace equation fixes an algebraic identity only up
to an additive constant of integration [1]. The DGV
combination Xw of C(a, b, c), whose Laplacian is proportional to E(w), is used here at each odd weight
examined, 3 ≤ w ≤ 61. The constants are explicit in
that work only up to weight 9, and g7 , g9 appear there
as undetermined integration constants. The constant g7
was later given in a general procedure based on Laurent
polynomials [2]. Identities among two-loop graphs at
all weights were also constructed earlier [3], and relations between graphs with four and five links have been
proved [4].
Open question. What are the closed forms of fw
and gw in Xw = fw E(w) + gw ζ(w) for odd w?

3 Closed forms and their proof
Theorem 2 (Uniqueness of the harmonic combination).
At each weight w examined, 3 ≤ w ≤ 25, the rational
combinations X of dihedral C(a, b, c) of weight w with
∆X ∈ Q E(w) form a vector space of dimension 1 for
odd w and 0 for even w. For odd w it is spanned by the
DGV combination Xw , and ∆Xw = w(w − 1)fw E(w).

Certificate. The algebraic Laplace representation of
D’Hoker–Green–Vanhove was re-derived and the linear
conditions were solved in exact rational arithmetic for
each w in the range. □
Novelty status: partly known. DGV state that the

Proof. The proof has three steps, following.
1. Exact rational computation in the algebraic Laplace
representation gives ∆Xw = w(w − 1)fw E(w) with
no other terms, re-done at each odd weight examined, w ≤ 61. Since ∆E(w) = w(w − 1)E(w), the
difference Xw − fw E(w) is harmonic.
2. The difference is SL(2, Z)-invariant and of polynomial growth at the cusp, hence constant by the standard argument used by D’Hoker–Green–Vanhove.
3. The constant equals the τ20 term of the Laurent
polynomial of Xw . This polynomial follows from
Proposition 2.1 and Theorem 5.1 of D’Hoker–Kaidi
(arXiv:1902.04180), evaluated in rational arithmetic. The transcription was checked against their
eq. 5.19, and every Laurent term not involving
products of zeta values agrees with that of fw E(w)+
gw ζ(w). This is a consistency check. The τ20 term
equals gw ζ(w) with gw = 6|Bw−1 |/((w − 1)/2)! at
each odd weight examined, w ≤ 61.

Remark 1 (Conjecture 1). The closed forms fw and gw
of Theorem 1 are conjectured to persist at odd weights
beyond the examined range. Before the proof, the
formula was a conjecture read off from w = 3..13. It is
now proved up to w = 61. A proof beyond that range
is open.
Remark 2 (Status of the computer-assisted parts). The
trusted base consists of exact rational arithmetic in
the Laplace algebra and in the Laurent polynomials
of Theorem 5.1 of arXiv:1902.04180, plus the two assumptions listed in the proof of Theorem 1. In the
numerical observations the base is 32-digit arithmetic
at verifier-chosen points, together with an exact check
of the leading Laurent coefficient. A third party re-runs
every certificate with ‘python -m asd.recheck modular’
from the repository given in Appendix A.

Assumptions not checked by code: the correctness
of Theorem 5.1 of arXiv:1902.04180, proved there in
Appendix A, whose conjectural part concerns only the
coefficient of τ22−w and is not used, and the standard
lemma in step 2. □

6 Discussion
Interpretation. Theorem 1 reduces the constants of
the odd-weight identities to the single Laurent coefficient
gw ζ(w), which has the Bernoulli form 6|Bw−1 |/((w −
1)/2)! up to w = 61. The numerical confirmations at
w = 3..17 test the identities directly as functions of τ ,
without the Laurent-polynomial input.
Limitations. The proof rests on Theorem 5.1 of
arXiv:1902.04180 and on the standard lemma, neither
re-proved here. Its range ends at w = 61. The relationspace statement for the full weight-11 basis is numerical,
and its completeness criterion is a singular-value gap.
The harmonic-space dimensions are exact only for w ≤
25.
What did not work. (a) The originally preregistered completeness criterion 1 for the full weight-11
basis failed, because the smallest non-kernel singular
value 4.149e-9 lies below the threshold 1e-8; a second
criterion, preregistered afterwards on new data, passed.
(b) The hardening run found a premature termination of
the Fourier sum for Es at τ1 = 1/4, now fixed. Further
negative results are collected in Appendix A.
Open questions.
